nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ إِلاَّ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ بَصَآئِرََ﴾.
It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — Allah's mercy be upon him — that he read ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ﴾ with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, and said: "By Allah, Pharaoh did not know; it was only Moses who knew."
Abū Jaʿfar said: All the readers read it with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, except al-Kisāʾī, who gave it a ḍamma. Had the ḥadīth from ʿAlī — may Allah have mercy on him — been sound, there would be no need for any deliberation on this, and that reading would be preferable; but it was only narrated by Abū Isḥāq, from a man of Murād, from ʿAlī — Allah's mercy be upon him.
Pharaoh's knowing it makes the proof against him stronger. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās argued for this with a decisive proof, saying: It is only ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ﴾ ("you [Pharaoh] have known"), just as the Exalted said: ﴿وَجَحَدُوا بِهَا وَاسْتَيْقَنَتْهَا أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ ("and they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them").
Ibrāhīm ibn Sharīk narrated to us; he said: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus narrated to us; he said: Zuhayr narrated to us; he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to us; he said: I heard Abū ʿUbayda ask Saʿd ibn ʿIyāḍ about the saying of the Exalted ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾. Saʿd said: It is like a man saying to his companion while arguing with him: "You surely know (لقد علِمْتَ)."
Zuhayr said: Abū Isḥāq said: And a man of Murād told me that he heard ʿAlī say: "By Allah, the enemy of Allah did not know; rather it was Moses who knew. He said: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ﴾ — I [have known] — and then said: ﴿وَإِنِّي لأَظُنُّكَ يٰفِرْعَونُ مَثْبُوراً﴾."
Al-Minhāl related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [مثبوراً means] cursed.
Ibn Jurayj related from Mujāhid that he said: perishing.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda that he said: destroyed.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: cursed.
Juwaybir related from him [al-Ḍaḥḥāk] that he said: perishing.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These sayings all come back to one thing, because the lexicographers report: «ما ثَبَرك عن هذا؟», i.e. "What held you back from this and turned you away from it?" So the meaning is: one held back from good.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأَرَادَ أَن يَسْتَفِزَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِِ﴾.
That is, to remove them from it, either by killing or by expulsion.

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ ٱسْكُنُواْ ٱلأَرْضَ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلآخِرَةِ جِئْنَا بِكُمْ لَفِيفاً﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, all together.
Sufyān related from Manṣūr from Abū Razīn that he said: From every people.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is preferable according to the lexicographers, because one says «لففتُ الشيءَ» ("I wrapped the thing together") when you have mixed it.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: «اللفيف» is a plural that has no singular, and it is like «الجميع» ("all together").

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلاَّ مُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً﴾.
That is, you give glad tidings of Paradise to the obedient and warn the disobedient of the Fire.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُرْآناً فَرَقْنَاهُ﴾.
Abū ʿAmr — may Allah have mercy on him — said: ﴿فَرَقْنَاهُ﴾: We made it clear.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿لِتَقْرَأَهُ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, with deliberateness.

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ يَخِرُّونَ لِلأَذْقَانِ سُجَّداًً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, upon the foreheads.
Qatāda said: That is, upon the faces.
And «الذَّقن» according to the lexicographers is the point where the two jawbones meet, and it is the part of the face nearest to the ground when prostration begins.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلِ ٱدْعُواْ ٱللَّهَ أَوِ ٱدْعُواْ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنََ﴾.
It is related that they said: "Do we call upon two?" So Allah, Majestic is His majesty, made known that none other than He is called upon by His names, and said: ﴿أَيّاً مَّا تَدْعُواْ فَلَهُ ٱلأَسْمَآءَ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَجْهَرْ بِصَلاَتِكَ وَلاَ تُخَافِتْ بِهَا وَٱبْتَغِ بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ سَبِيلاً﴾.
There are two views on it:
The first: al-Aʿmash related it from Jaʿfar ibn Iyās, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite aloud when he recited, and the idolaters would revile the Qurʾān, the One who sent it down and the one who brought it; so he began to recite quietly. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَلاَ تَجْهَرْ بِصَلاَتِكَ وَلاَ تُخَافِتْ بِهَا﴾.
The other view: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa related it from his father, who said: ʿĀʾisha said to me: "O son of my sister, do you know concerning what ﴿وَلاَ تَجْهَرْ بِصَلاَتِكَ وَلاَ تُخَافِتْ بِهَا﴾ was sent down?" He said: I said: "No." She said: "It was sent down concerning supplication (al-duʿāʾ)."
Abū Jaʿfar said: Both chains of transmission are good. Supplication is called «صلاة», whereas this hardly ever applies to recitation. Al-Aʿshā said:
تَقُولُ بِنْتِي وَقَدْ قَرَّبْتُ مُرْتَحِــلاً * يَا رَبِّ جَنِّبْ أبِي الأَوْصَابَا والوَجَعَا
(My daughter says, as I have brought near my mount for departure: "O Lord, keep my father away from ailments and pain.")
عَلَيْكِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي صَلَّيْتِ فَاغْتَمِضِي * نَوْمَــاً فَإِنَّ لِجَنْبِ المَرْءِ مُضْطَجَعَاً
(Upon you be the like of what you have prayed for; so close your eyes in sleep, for a man's side must have a place to lie down.)
It is also said: It is called «صلاة» only because it does not take place without supplication; supplication is «صلاة», so it was named after it.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَم يَكُنْ لَّهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي ٱلْمُلْكِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ وَلِيٌّ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّ﴾.
That is, He has no need of anyone to come to His aid.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيراً﴾.
That is, magnify Him with great magnification.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, exalted be His majesty: ﴿سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلاًً﴾.
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the meaning of ﴿سُبْحَانَ﴾ and he said: declaring Allah far removed from evil.
And in one ḥadīth: Allah's being free of evil.
Sībawayh and others said: its meaning is Allah's being free of evil; and he recited:
أَقُولُ لمَّا جَاءنِي فَخْرُهُ * سُبْحَانَ من عَلْقَمَةَ الفَاخِرِ
(I say, when his boasting reached me: how far removed [I am] from ʿAlqama the boaster!)
Maʿmar narrated from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama, from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I stood in the Ḥijr when my people disbelieved me [about] the night I was taken on the night journey; I praised my Lord and asked Him to set (Bayt al-Maqdis) before me, and it was raised up for me, and I began describing its signs to them."
Sufyān narrated from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father, from Abū Dharr, that he said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was established first? He said: al-Masjid al-Ḥarām. I said: then which? He said: then al-Masjid al-Aqṣā. I said: how long between them? He said: forty years. Then he said: wherever the prayer comes upon you, pray, for it is a mosque."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلأَقْصَى ٱلَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ﴾.
﴿مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾ means Mecca; ﴿إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلأَقْصَى﴾ means Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem); ﴿ٱلَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ﴾ — it has been said: He made rivers gush forth around it and caused fruits to grow.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَآ إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلبَصِيرُ﴾.
﴿لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَآ﴾: what he saw of the prophets and their traces.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَآ مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَاهُ هُدًى لِّبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
That is: We guided them by it to right guidance.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَلاَّ تَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِي وَكِيلاً﴾.
It is also read ﴿أَنْ لاَ يتَّخِذُوا﴾, with something implied (iḍmār), meaning: and We enjoined upon them.
Warqāʾ narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ: ﴿أَلاَّ تَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِي وَكِيلاً﴾ — he said: a partner.
Abū Jaʿfar said: that is well known in the language: it is said of everyone who stands in the place of another in anything whatsoever: he is his partner.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿أَلاَّ تَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِي وَكِيلاً﴾, i.e. one who suffices.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍٍ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: it is in the vocative (al-nidāʾ), i.e. "O (أَيْ) offspring of those We carried".
Abū Jaʿfar said: "أَيْ" is a vocative particle like "يا".
Sufyān narrated from Ḥumayd, from Mujāhid, that he read ﴿ذَرِّيةَ﴾ with fatḥa on the dhāl and doubling of the rāʾ and the yāʾ.
It is narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit ﴿ذِرِّيةَ﴾, with kasra on the dhāl and doubling of the rāʾ and the yāʾ.
As for ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid, he related that Zayd read ﴿ذَرِّيةََ﴾ with fatḥa on the dhāl and doubling of the rāʾ and the yāʾ.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَبْداً شَكُوراً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: "When he put on a garment he would say: 'In the name of Allah', and when he took it off he would say: 'Praise be to Allah'."
Maʿmar narrated from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, that he said: his thankfulness was that when he ate he would say: In the name of Allah, and when he had finished eating he would say: Praise be to Allah.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِِ﴾.
Sufyān said: i.e. upon the Children of Israel.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿قَضَيْنَا﴾: We informed.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ أُولاهُمَا﴾.
That is: the first of the two times.
﴿بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَاداً لَّنَآ أُوْلِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: they came from the direction of Persia the first time, and with them was "Nebuchadnezzar (Bukhtanaṣṣar)", and the Children of Israel defeated them; then they returned the second time, killed the Children of Israel and destroyed them utterly.
Qatāda said: He sent against them the first time "Jālūt (Goliath)", and the second time "Bukhtanaṣṣar".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَجَاسُواْ خِلاَلَ ٱلدِّيَارِ وَكَانَ وَعْداً مَّفْعُولاً﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: ﴿جَاسُوا﴾: they walked.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what is well known among the lexicographers is that one says «جُسْنَا دُورَ بنِي فلانٍ» and «جِسْنَاها» when they have overpowered and vanquished them.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ ٱلْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, i.e. the turn of power; ﴿وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُم بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيراً﴾.
It is possible that ﴿نَفِيرَاً﴾ means «نافر» (one who sets out), like «قدير» and «قادر».
And it is possible that it is the plural of «نَفْر», like «عَبِيد», «كَلِيب» and «مَعِيز»; and its origin is [from] those of a man's clan and companions who set out with him.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾.
﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e. [the last] of the two times; ﴿لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾.
Zāʾida narrated from al-Aʿmash that he said: [i.e.] Allah, so that He may disgrace your faces.
Someone else said: so that the promise may disgrace your faces.
It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read ﴿لنسوءَ وجوهكم﴾ with nūn, and that is the reading of al-Kisāʾī; there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: so when the promise of the last came, We sent them so that We might disgrace your faces.
It is narrated from Ubayy [ibn] Kaʿb that he read ﴿فإذا جاء وعدُ الآخرة لَنَسُوءَنْ وجوهَكُمْ﴾ with the light nūn [of emphasis] and the lām with fatḥa; the pause on it is «لنسوءَا», like «لنسفَعَا»; and this involves no omission.
Whoever read ﴿لِيسُوءُوا﴾, the meaning for him refers to the servants, and there is an omission in it.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوْاْ تَتْبِيراً﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said: so that they may destroy utterly; Ibn ʿAbbās said the same.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and so it is in the language; one says «تَبَّر الشيءَ» when he has broken it, and from it comes «التِّبْر» (gold dust).

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَإِنْ عُدتُّمْ عُدْنَا﴾.
Mubārak narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: "If you return to disobedience, We will return to punishment."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ حَصِيراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. they are confined in it.
Al-Ḥasan said: a bed and a place of return.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: a prison.
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is well known in the language that one says «حصرتُ الرجل», i.e. I confined him; and the place in which one is confined is called «حَصِير»; and one says «أحصَرَه المرضُ» (illness confined him); and the root in it is one.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ يَِهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُُ﴾.
[The meaning is: it guides to the state that is most upright]; and the state that is most upright is affirming the Oneness of Allah, following His messengers, and acting in obedience to Him.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَدْعُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ بِٱلشَّرِّ دُعَآءَهُ بِٱلْخَيْرِ وَكَانَ ٱلإِنْسَانُ عَجُولاً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: man prays against himself for something which, were it granted to him, he would perish; and he prays against his child and his wealth.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱلإِنْسَانُ عَجُولاً﴾ — it has been said: he hastens to pray against himself, but Allah does not hasten to answer.
It is narrated from Salmān that he said: the first of Ādam that Allah created was his head, and he began looking at the rest of himself being created; and when evening drew near he said: [My Lord, hasten] before nightfall. So Allah said: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱلإِنْسَانُ عَجُولاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلْلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ آيَتَيْنِ﴾.
«الآية» in the language is an indication and a sign, i.e. We made them both indicate that their Creator has nothing like Him, and indicate the number of years and the reckoning.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَمَحَوْنَآ آيَةَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَآ آيَةَ ٱلنَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً﴾.
Hushaym narrated from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَمَحَوْنَآ آيَةَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ — he said: it is the dark patch which you see on the moon.
It is narrated that Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked "ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib" about the dark patch on the moon, and he said: if only you would ask about what benefits you in your world and your Hereafter! That is because Allah says: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلْلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ آيَتَيْنِ﴾ to the end of the verse; the sign of the day is the sun, and the sign of the night is the moon, and its «صَحْو» is the dark patch which is in it.
[Translator's note: «صَحْوُهُ» as printed; the sense of the passage requires «مَحْوُهُ», "its erasing".]
And His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا آيَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصَرِةً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan narrated from Qatāda that he said: shining.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, for he said that ﴿مُبْصِرَةً﴾ means: giving light.
Someone else said: this is by way of likening, i.e. possessing sight, i.e. they see by it.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَآئِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِِ﴾.
Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Najīḥ and Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujāhid that he said: his deeds.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: his provision, his term, his misery and his happiness.
Ibn Jurayj narrated from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: ﴿طائرة﴾ is what has been decreed for him; it is with him wherever he is, and moves away with him wherever he moves.
It has also been said: ﴿طَائِرُهُ﴾ is his lot.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meanings are close to one another; it is only what flies [to him] of good or evil, by way of figurative likening, as you say: "this is on So-and-so's neck", i.e. it clings to him as a necklace clings.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ كِتَاباً يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُوراً﴾.
Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated from Ḥumayd, from Mujāhid, that he read ﴿وَيُخْرِجُ لهُ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ كِتَاباً﴾, and said: he means: and the ṭāʾir (lot) will bring out for him a book, i.e. his deeds as a book.
It is narrated from Mujāhid ﴿ويُخْرَجُ﴾, and so Abū Jaʿfar "Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ" read.
Al-Ḥasan read: «ويَخْرَجُ له يوم القيامة كتاباً», also with fatḥa on the yāʾ.
This reading is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, for he said: his deeds will be turned into a book.
Al-Ḥasan read ﴿يُلَقَّاهُ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ and doubling of the qāf.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولاًً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, that he said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather the people of the interval (ahl al-fatra), the feeble-minded, the deaf, the dumb, the mute, and the old men who did not live to see Islam; and He will send a messenger to them [saying]: Enter the Fire. They will say: How, when no messenger came to us? — he said: and if they had entered it, it would have been coolness and safety for them — then Allah will send a messenger to them, and whoever wanted to obey Him will obey him. Then Abū Hurayra recited ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولاً﴾."
Someone else said: the Day of Resurrection is not a day of religious obligation nor of trial, such that a messenger would be sent to anyone; rather, the meaning of the verse is: and We would not punish anyone in this world with destruction until We had sent a messenger.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَآ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نُّهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُواْ فِيهَا﴾.
This word is read in several ways:
It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read ﴿أَمَرْنَا﴾ with a short vowel and without doubling, and the same is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās.
It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read ﴿أَمَّرْنَا مُتْرَفِيها﴾, and so read Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī and Abū al-ʿĀliya.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿آامَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها﴾.
And ﴿أَمِرْنَا مُتْرفيها﴾, on the pattern faʿilnā, is narrated; this reading too is from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever reads ﴿أَمَرْنَا مُتْرفيها﴾, there are three views about his reading:
One of them, and the soundest, is what Ibn Jurayj said — and he claimed it is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās — namely that the meaning is: We commanded them to obedience, but they acted corruptly.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: it is known that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commands only justice and excellence, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يأمُر بالعَدْلِ وَالإِحْسَانِ﴾; so it is known that the meaning is: We commanded its affluent ones to obedience, but they disobeyed.
Mujāhid said: (its affluent ones) are its corrupt ones.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: its arrogant ones.
And the meaning is: We commanded them to obedience — and the corrupt one, when commanded to obedience, disobeys — so they disobeyed, and the word became due against them on account of disobedience, i.e. it became binding.
The second view on the meaning of ﴿أَمَرْنا﴾ is: We made [them] many.
Al-Kisāʾī said: it is possible that "أَمَرْنا" means "أمَّرنا", from imāra (authority); and he rejected that "أَمَرْنا" could mean "We made many", and said: in this sense one says only «آمَرْنَا».
Abū Jaʿfar said: this third view — I mean the view of al-Kisāʾī — is rejected by the lexicographers.
Abū Zayd and Abū ʿUbayda have related that one says "أَمَرْنَا" meaning "We made many".
This is supported by the ḥadīth traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ): (The best property is a row of pollinated palms (sikka maʾbūra) and a fertile mare (muhra maʾmūra)).
«السِّكَّة المأبورة» is pollinated palm trees, and «المُهْرة المأمورة» is one with abundant offspring.
As for the meaning of ﴿أَمَّرْنا﴾, there are two views about it:
One of them was narrated by Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿أمَّرْنَا﴾: We gave power over [them]. Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī said the same.
Wakīʿ narrated from Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliya, that he read ﴿أَمَّرْنا﴾ with doubling, i.e. We gave power to its arrogant ones.
The second view: al-Kisāʾī narrated it from Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliya: ﴿أَمَّرْنَا﴾, i.e. We made [them] many.
What al-Kisāʾī narrated is not «بمعبد» [far-fetched], and it would be like «سَمِنَ الدَّابةُ» (the beast grew fat), «سَمَّنتُه» and «أسمنتُه» (I fattened it).
[Translator's note: «بمعبدٍ» as printed; the sense requires «ببعيدٍ», "far-fetched".]
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is more fitting; He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said ﴿فَفَسَقُواْ فِيهَا﴾, describing them as a group, and a single town is not described as having in it a group of rulers.
If it is said: it could be one [ruler], it has been answered: this is a specification, and destruction comes through great numbers, so that acts of disobedience become many.
As for the meaning of "ءآمَرْنَا", it is likewise "We made many".
Al-Ḥasan said: and "آمرنا" may mean: We increased their «عَدَهُم» and increased their wealth; and the true sense of «أَمِرَ» is: his possessions of wealth, or of anything else of his condition, became many; and from it is ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئَاً إِمْرَاً﴾.
[Translator's note: «عَدَهُمْ» as printed; probably «عددهم», "their number".]
Al-Kisāʾī said: [«إمراً» means] something grave.
Hārūn said that in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿وَإِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً بَعَثْنا فيها أكَابِرَ مجرميها، فمكَرُوا فيها، فحقَّ عليها القَوْلُ﴾.
As for the meaning of "آمَرْنَا" [sic], it is scarcely known, because one only says «أَمِرَ القومُ» when they have become many, and «آمرَهُمُ اللهُ», i.e. He made them many; and «أَمِرَهُم اللهُ» is not known.
[Translator's note: from the reasoning that follows, the form said to be scarcely known is evidently «أَمِرْنا» (faʿilnā), not «آمَرْنا»; the text is translated as written.]

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَآءُ﴾.
﴿ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ﴾, i.e. this world; ﴿عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَآءُ﴾ — and it is also read "ما يَشاءُ" (what he/He wills).
Abū Jaʿfar said: the two meanings are one, i.e. what Allah wills.
And it is possible that it refers to (مَنْ) [i.e. what the one who desires wills].
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلاهَا مَذْمُوماً مَّدْحُوراً﴾.
That is: driven far away. One says «دَحَرَه، يدْحَرُه، دَحْراً، ودُحُوراً» when he has driven him away.
Then He, the Exalted, informed that He provides for the believer and the disbeliever, and said: ﴿كُلاً نُمِدُّ هَؤُلاَءِ وَهَؤُلاَءِ مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلاَّ تَعْبُدُوۤاْ إِلاَّ إِيَّاهُ﴾.
Mubārak narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: ﴿قَضَى﴾: He commanded that you worship none but Him.
Sufyān narrated from al-Aʿmash that he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read "ووصَّى ربُّك ألاَّ تعبدوا إلا إيَّاه" (and your Lord has enjoined that you worship none but Him).
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾.
That is: and He commanded that you do good to parents with goodness.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ﴾.
It is narrated from Mujāhid that he said: do not find them filthy, just as they did not find you filthy.
The meaning according to the lexicographers is: do not find them burdensome, and do not speak harshly to them; people say of what they find burdensome: "أفٍّ له" (uff to it).
The origin of this is that when dust or something that bothers a person falls on him, he blows on it and says: «أُفّ».
It has also been said that «أفّ» is the dirt of the fingernails, and that «التُّفّ» is something contemptible, such as the dirt of the ear; but the first view is better known.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَنْهَرْهُمَا﴾, i.e. do not speak to them with shouting nor with irritation.
One says «نَهَره» and «انتَهَره» with one meaning.
He made this clear by His saying ﴿وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلاً كَرِيماًً﴾.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read ﴿وَاخْفِضْ لهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذِّلِّ من الرَّحْمةِ﴾ with kasra on the dhāl.
The meaning with ḍamma [al-dhull] is: be towards them like one who is lowly and overpowered, out of honour, reverence and veneration.
Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated from his father — and some say from ʿĀʾisha —: ﴿وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ﴾: it is that he obeys them and does not refuse anything they want.
ʿAṭāʾ said: do not raise your hand against them.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: it is [like] the speech of a sinful slave to a rough, harsh master.
One says «ذَلَّ، يَذِلُّ، ذُلاً، وذِلَّةً، ومَذَلَّةً», and he is «ذالّ» and «ذليل».
The meaning of «الذِّلّ» with kasra is: being yielding towards them; one says «رجلٌ ذليلٌ بيِّنُ الذِّلِّ» when he is yielding, gentle and compliant.
Likewise one says «دابَّةٌ ذَلُولٌ بَيِّنُ الذِّلِّ» when it is compliant; and from it is ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ إِن تَكُونُواْ صَالِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ لِلأَوَّابِينَ غَفُوراً﴾.
Shuʿba narrated from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he said: «الأوَّابون» are those who return to good,
as in the saying of Allah: ﴿إنَّه أوَّابٌ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: it was read before al-Firyābī, from Qutayba, who said: Ibn Lahīʿa narrated to us, from Abū Hubayra, from Ḥanash ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: «الأوَّاب» is the mindful one (al-ḥafīẓ) who, when he remembers his sins, seeks forgiveness for them.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إنَّهُ كَانَ لَلأَوَّابِينَ غَفُوَراً﴾, that he said: they are those who remember their sins in private, then seek Allah's forgiveness.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib: ﴿الأَوَّابُ﴾ is the one who sins then repents, then sins then repents, then sins then repents.
Abū Jaʿfar said: these views are close to one another; the root of this is that one says «آبَ، يئوبُ» when he returns, so he is «آيب», and «أوَّاب» is [the form] of intensive frequency.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتِ ذَا ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ حَقَّهُُ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: i.e. the kindness with which you want to maintain ties with him.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَٱلْمِسْكِينَ وَٱبْنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَلاَ تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيراً﴾.
Ḥuṣayn narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: «التبذير» (squandering) is spending in other than the obedience of Allah.
The same is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
﴿إنَّ المبَذِّرينَ كانُوا إخْوَانَ الشَّيَاطِينِ﴾.
The meaning of "the brothers of the devils" is: in disobedience.
Since they disobeyed and those [devils] disobeyed, disobedience united them, so they were called brothers; and whenever you join one thing to another, you have made them brothers; and from it is the Prophet's ﷺ establishing brotherhood among his Companions.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «إخاءُ النبي لله بين أصحابه»; «لله» appears to be a corruption of «ﷺ».]

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُل لَّهُمْ قَوْلاً مَّيْسُوراًً﴾.
Qatāda said: i.e. make them a promise.
ʿIkrima said: if you turn away from them because of provision you are waiting for, then make them a promise and say to them: it will come; when something comes to us we will give to you.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿قَوْلاً مَّيْسُوراً﴾, i.e. gentle.
The meaning according to the lexicographers is: make their poverty easy for them by your supplication for them.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلاَ تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ ٱلْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُوماً مَّحْسُوراًً﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَلاَ تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ﴾, i.e. do not refrain from spending in obedience; [﴿وَلاَ تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ ٱلْبَسْطِ﴾], i.e. do not spend in disobedience.
﴿فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُوماً مَّحْسُوراً﴾ — ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: i.e. regretful.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُوماً﴾ — he said: sinful or guilty; ﴿مَّحْسُوراً﴾: left stranded.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and so is «المحسور» in the language; one says «حَسَره السَّفَرُ» when the journey has left him stranded; and likewise a camel is «حسير» and «محسور» when it is worn out and stops, and that is more severe than fatigue.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوۤاْ أَوْلادَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلاقٍٍ﴾.
«الإملاق» is poverty; and they used to bury their daughters alive.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطآءً كَبِيراً﴾.
With kasra on the khāʾ and the long vowel.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan: "كَانَ خَطَاءً", with fatḥa on the khāʾ and the long vowel.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best known of these readings among the lexicographers is ﴿كان خِطْأً كَبِيرَاً﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said — and he claimed it is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās — and it is the view of Mujāhid: «الخِطْء» is sin.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is what is well known in the language; one says «خَطِئَ، يَخْطأُ، خِطْأً» when he has sinned and committed the wrong deliberately; and «خَطْأً» has also been related as the maṣdar (verbal noun).
And «أخطَأ، يُخْطِىءُ، إخطاءً», the noun being «الخَطَأ», [is said] when he did not commit the wrong deliberately.
As for the reading of whoever read "كان خِطَاء" with kasra and the long vowel, and [with] fatḥa and the long vowel, it is not known in the language nor in the speech of the Arabs.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ بِٱلحَقِّ﴾.
The ḥadīth explained this: (The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except for one of three things: associating others [with Allah] after faith, adultery after iḥṣān (being married), or killing a soul without [right of retaliation for] a soul).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظْلُوماً فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَاناً﴾.
The early scholars differed about the "authority" (al-sulṭān) that was given to the next of kin (al-walī).
Khuṣayf narrated from Mujāhid that he said: his proof [i.e. right] which was given to him is that he may kill his killer.
A group of scholars held that this is the authority given to him, and that he may not take the blood-money (al-diya) unless the killer wishes.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said about the authority given to him: if he wishes he kills, if he wishes he takes the blood-money, and if he wishes he pardons.
The view of the people of Medina and the people of Kufa is the view of Mujāhid: that the authority here is retaliation (al-qawad) specifically, not anything else.
Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, held the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, except that he said: if he pardons he is entitled to take the blood-money, whether he stipulated it or not; and his proof is ﴿فَمَنْ عُفِي لهُ منْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ﴾,
and the ḥadīth: "The next of kin of the slain has [the better] of two options."
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ يُسْرِف فِّي ٱلْقَتْلِ﴾.
Khuṣayf narrated from Mujāhid that he said: let him not kill anyone other than his killer.
Manṣūr narrated from Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb that he said: do not kill anyone other than your killer, and do not mutilate him.
Khuṣayf narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he said: two are not to be killed for one.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: let him not kill the killer's father or his son.
Ḥudhayfa read ﴿فَلاَ تُسْرِفْ فِي القَتْلِ﴾ with tāʾ.
Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm narrated from Mujāhid that he said: it is [addressed] to the first killer.
On this basis the meaning for him is: so do not go to excess, O killer.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُوراً﴾.
Ibn Kathīr narrated from Mujāhid that he said: "The slain one is helped; and the meaning of His saying is that Allah helped him through his next of kin."
It is narrated that in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿فلا تُسْرِفُوا فِي القَتْلِ﴾ «إنَّ وليَّ المقتول كان منصوراً» (indeed the next of kin of the slain is helped).
Abū Jaʿfar said: the clearest is with yāʾ, and it refers to the next of kin, because "let him not go to excess" is said only to one who has the right to kill, and this is the next of kin.
It may also be with tāʾ, and also refer to the next of kin, except that it then requires a shift in the address.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبُواْ مَالَ ٱلْيَتِيمِ إِلاَّ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُُ﴾.
Muḥammad [ibn Sīrīn] said: I asked ʿAbīda about His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ فَقِيرَاً فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾.
He said: he borrows, and when he becomes rich he repays; then he recited ﴿فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أمْوَالَهُمْ فأَشْهِدُوا عليهِمْ﴾.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said something similar to this.
And ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Allah's mercy be upon him, said what supports this.
Abū Jaʿfar "Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Naḥwī" narrated to us; he said: al-Ḥasan ibn Ghulayb narrated to us; he said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAdī narrated to us; he said: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Yarfaʾ, the client of ʿUmar, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: O Yarfaʾ, I have placed Allah's wealth, in relation to me, in the position of an orphan's wealth: when I am in need I take from it, and when I am well off I repay it; and if I am free of need I refrain from it; for I have been entrusted with a mighty matter of the affairs of the Muslims.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: not even water is to be drunk from the orphan's wealth. He [the narrator] said: I said to him: but Allah says ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ فَقِيرَاً فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾? He said: that is only for his serving him and washing his clothes.
Abū Yaḥyā and Layth narrated from Mujāhid that he said: do not approach the orphan's wealth except for trade, and do not borrow [from it]. He said: as for His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ فَقِيرَاً فَلْيَأكُلْ بالمَعْرُوفِ﴾, its meaning is only: let him eat from his wealth in a fitting manner, meaning from his own wealth.
A group of the jurists and the people of reasoning held this, so much so that Abū Yūsuf said: perhaps His saying ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ غنِيَّاً فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ وَمَنْ كَانَ فَقِيراً فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ is abrogated by His saying ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَأْكُلُوا أمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالبَاطِِل﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ﴾.
The explanation of this is in His saying ﴿حَتَّى إذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. puberty.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا ٱلْكَيْلَ إِذا كِلْتُمْ وَزِنُواْ بِٱلقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujāhid that he said: «القِسْطاس» is justice.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is the balance.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: i.e. better in outcome,
i.e. what the matter leads to, in this world and the Hereafter.
It has also been said: better than short measure.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌٌ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: do not say what you have no knowledge of. ﴿إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولـٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُولاً﴾ — he said: it will be asked: did that happen or not?
Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, Allah's mercy be upon him, said: this is about false testimony.
Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, that he said: ﴿لاَ تَقْفُ﴾: do not accuse.
Abū Jaʿfar said: these views come back to one meaning, and it is from «قَفَوتُ الشيءَ», i.e. I followed its trace; and the meaning is: do not make your tongue follow what you do not know, so that you speak by guesswork and conjecture.
Al-Kisāʾī related: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْفُ﴾ is from «القيافة» (tracking), and it has the same meaning as the first, by metathesis (ʿalā al-qalb).

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَمْشِ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مَرَحاًً﴾.
That is: arrogant and haughty.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَن تَخْرِقَ ٱلأَرْضَ وَلَن تَبْلُغَ ٱلْجِبَالَ طُولاً﴾.
The lexicographers have two views about it.
One of them: that the meaning is: you will not bore through the earth.
And the other: you will not traverse all of it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is clearer, as if it were taken from «الخَرْق», which is the vast desert.
And one says: «فلانٌ أخرقُ من فلانٍ», i.e. he travels and goes on raids more than he does.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿كُلُّ ذٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً﴾.
It is also read ﴿سَيِّئَةً عندَ ربِّكَ مَكْروهَاً﴾.
It has been said: the first is clearer, because His saying ﴿وَآتِ ذَا القُرْبَى حَقَّهُ﴾ preceded, along with things good and evil; so He said ﴿كُلُّ ذٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً﴾.
And also, He did not say «مكروهةً» (feminine).

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ذَلِكَ مِمَّآ أَوْحَىٰ إِلَيْكَ رَبُّكَ مِنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلاَ تَجْعَلْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهاً آخَرَ فَتُلْقَىٰ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَلُوماً مَّدْحُوراً﴾.
That is: banished and driven far away; and from it is "O Allah, drive Satan away from us (ادحَرْ عنَّا الشيطان)".

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَفَأَصْفَاكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِٱلْبَنِينَ وَٱتَّخَذَ مِنَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ إِنَاثاً﴾.
Because they said: the angels are the daughters of Allah — exalted is Allah [above that].

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ لَّوْ كَانَ مَعَهُ آلِهَةٌ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذاً لاَّبْتَغَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ذِي ٱلْعَرْشِ سَبِيلاًً﴾.
Qatāda said: the meaning is: then they would have sought nearness to Allah.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: then they would have sought a way to reach Him, in order to remove His dominion, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾.
It has been said: its glorification is its being an indication of Allah's power and that He is its Creator.
Most of the exegetes, among them ʿIkrima, hold that the meaning is: and there is nothing having a soul but that it glorifies Him with praise.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is more fitting, because He said ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرآنَ جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ حِجَاباً مَّسْتُوراً﴾.
There are two views about it:
One of them: that the veil is the sealing of their hearts; and this is indicated by ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقهُوهُ﴾.
The other view: that the veil is Allah's protecting him from them.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا ذَكَرْتَ رَبَّكَ فِي ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَحْدَهُ وَلَّوْاْ عَلَىٰ أَدْبَارِهِمْ نُفُوراً﴾.
Abū al-Jawzāʾ said: the remembrance is saying "There is no god but Allah".

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَسْتَمِعُونَ بِهِ إِذْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوَىٰ﴾.
That is: people of najwa, i.e. of secret talk.
Then He made clear what they were whispering about, and said, exalted be His praise:
﴿إِذْ يَقُولُ ٱلظَّالِمُونَ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ رَجُلاً مَّسْحُوراً﴾.
There are two views about its meaning:
Mujāhid said: i.e. deceived.
Abū ʿUbayda said: i.e. having a «سَحْر»; and «السَّحْر» and «السُّحْر» are the lung.
And the meaning according to him is: "you follow only a human being", i.e. not an angel.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is more suited to the meaning and better known in the speech of the Arabs, because one says: "So-and-so is nothing but «مسحور»", i.e. deceived, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿إنِّي لأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسَى مَسْحُورَاً﴾,
i.e. deceived. The poet said:
أَرَانَا مُوضِعِينَ لِحَتْم غَيْبٍ * وَنُسْخَرُ بالطَّعَامِ وبِالشَّرَابِ
(I see us hastening towards a hidden decree, while we are beguiled with food and drink.)
That is: we are distracted with them, so it is as if we are being deceived. And this is made clear by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لكَ الأَمْثَالَ﴾.
And He said in another place: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعلِّمهُ بَشَرٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُوۤاْ أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً وَرُفَاتاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. dust; and that is the view of al-Farrāʾ.
Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: from it one says «رُفِتَ رَفْتاً», i.e. it was crushed.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقاً جَدِيداً﴾? [verse 49].
That is: renewed.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ كُونُواْ حِجَارَةً أَوْ حَدِيداً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. be whatever you wish, you will be brought back.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a good view, because they cannot become stones; rather the meaning is that they had acknowledged their Creator and denied the resurrection, so it was said to them: imagine yourselves being whatever you wish; even if you were stones or iron, you would be resurrected just as you were created the first time.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَوْ خَلْقاً مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾.
That is: [what] seems great.
Ibn ʿUmar, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Abū Ṣāliḥ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿أَوْ خَلْقاً مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ ﴾: it is death.
And in the ḥadīth: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a black-and-white ram, and it will be slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire."
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ رُؤُوسَهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هُوَ﴾.
That is: they move them from top to bottom and from bottom to top, as one does who is astonished and thinks a thing slow in coming.
One says «أنغَضَ رأسَه فنَغَضَ، ينغَضُ، ويَنْغِضُ، ويَنْغُضُ», i.e. it moved.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِِ﴾.
Sufyān said: i.e. by His command.
And the meaning according to the exegetes is: acknowledging that He is your Creator.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُل لِّعِبَادِي يَقُولُواْ ٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَانَ يَنزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْْ﴾.
That is: he sows corruption and stirs up [strife].

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُولَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read ﴿أولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ يَبتَغُونَ إِلَى رَبِّهِمُ الوَسيلَةَ﴾ (with tāʾ: "those whom you call upon").
He said: "These were some Arabs who worshipped some people of the jinn; then the jinn became Muslim, and those who worshipped them did not know."
Shuʿba narrated from al-Suddī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿أُولَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ﴾, that he said: ʿĪsā and ʿUzayr.
It has also been said: the angels; those who worshipped them were a people of the Arabs.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوهَا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَاباً شَدِيداًً﴾.
Mujāhid said: [We shall] annihilate it or punish it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَانَ ذٰلِك فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ مَسْطُوراً﴾.
That is: written; one says «سَطَر» when he wrote.
It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "The first thing Allah created was the Pen; He said to it: Write; so it wrote what is to be."

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرْسِلَ بِٱلآيَاتِ إِلاَّ أَن كَذَّبَ بِهَا ٱلأَوَّلُونََ﴾.
This is a difficult verse, and there is an omission in the speech.
The meaning is: nothing prevented Us from sending the signs which you demanded, except that you would deny them and be destroyed, as was done with those before you.
And Allah has deferred the matter of this community until the Day of Resurrection, for He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿بَل السَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. a sign.
And the meaning is: possessing sight, by which one sees and by which the truthfulness of Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him, becomes clear.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَا وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِٱلآيَاتِ إِلاَّ تَخْوِيفا﴾.
That is: they did wrong by denying it.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
Shuʿba narrated from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan, that he said: He protected you from them.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: they are in His grasp.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا ٱلرُّؤيَا ٱلَّتِي أَرَيْنَاكَ إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً لِّلنَّاسِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is the vision which he saw on the night he was taken on the night journey.
ʿIkrima added: it was a vision in a waking state.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: ﴿إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً لِّلنَّاسِ﴾, i.e. only as a trial for people.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱلشَّجَرَةَ ٱلْمَلْعُونَةَ فِي ٱلقُرْآنِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is the tree of al-Zaqqūm.
Others said: people were tried by the vision and the tree of al-Zaqqūm only in that a group apostatised and said: how could he be taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis in a single night? And when Allah revealed ﴿إنَّ شَجَرَة الزقُّوم. طَعَامُ الأَثيم﴾ they said: how can there be a tree in the Fire without the Fire consuming it?
So that was a trial for some people and a means of insight for others, among them Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him.
And it is said that he was called al-Ṣiddīq (the affirmer of truth) only at that time.
If someone says: the cursing of this tree is not mentioned in the Qurʾān?
Abū Jaʿfar said: there are two answers to that:
One of them: that those who eat it have indeed been cursed.
And the other answer: that the Arabs say of every harmful, detested food: [cursed].

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيََّ﴾.
That is: You have preferred. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Tell me about this one whom You have preferred over me — why have You preferred him, when You created me from fire and created him from clay?! Then this was omitted because the hearer knows it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ لأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: most lexicographers hold that the meaning is: I shall surely take control [over them] and uproot them, from their saying «احتنَكَ الجرادُ الزرعَ» when the locusts have taken all of the crops.
It has also been said: it is from their saying «حَنَكَ الدابَّةَ يَحْنِكُها» when he ties a rope around its lower jaw and leads it; Ibn al-Sikkīt related that.
And «احتَنَكَ دابَّته» has also been related, like «حَنَكَ»; so the meaning would be: I shall surely lead them however I wish.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَ ٱذْهَبْ فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمْ جَزَاءً مَّوْفُوراً﴾.
«موفور» and «موفَّر» are the same; one says «وفَرْتُه» and «وَفَّرْتُه», as [the poet] said:
وَمَنْ يَجْعَلِ المَعْرُوفَ مَنْ دُونِ عِرْضِهِ * يَفِرْهُ وَمَنْ لاَ يَتَّقِي الشَّتْمَ يُشْتَم
(Whoever makes kindness a shield before his honour keeps it intact, and whoever does not guard against abuse is abused.)

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱسْتَفْزِزْ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتَ مِنْهُمْ بِصَوْتِكََ﴾.
That is: incite [them] lightly.
Mujāhid said: ﴿بصَوْتكَ﴾: with singing and pipes.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِم بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ وَشَارِكْهُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْوَالِ وَٱلأَوْلادِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: every horse that rode in disobedience to Allah, every foot that walked in disobedience to Allah, every wealth obtained unlawfully, and every child of fornication — it belongs to Satan.
Someone else said: his sharing in wealth is the sāʾiba and the baḥīra, and in children it is their saying: ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā and ʿAbd al-Ḥārith.
Qatāda read ﴿وأَجْلِبْ عليهمْ بخَيْلكَ ورِجَالِك﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَعِدْهُمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً﴾.
This is a command carrying the meaning of threat and warning, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فمنْ شَاءَ فَلْيؤمنْ، ومن شَاءَ فَلْيكفُرْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانٌٌ﴾.
It has been said: i.e. My sincere, chosen ones, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَادْخُلِي في عِبَادِي﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ وَكِيلاً﴾.
That is: as One who rescues His sincere ones from Satan.
Al-Farrāʾ holds that the meaning of ﴿وَكِيلاً﴾ is "sufficient", and he said the same about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿أَلاَّ تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِي وَكِيلاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿رَّبُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي يُزْجِي لَكُمُ ٱلْفُلْكَ﴾.
That is: He drives.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَأَمِنْتُمْ أَن يَخْسِفَ بِكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلْبَرِّ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِباًً﴾.
«الحاصب» is the wind that pelts with «الحَصْباء», which is small pebbles.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ أَن يُعِيدَكُمْ فِيهِ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ فَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ قَاصِفاً مِّنَ ٱلرِّيحِِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is the one that drowns.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says «قَصَفَه» when he has broken it, as if, from its violence, it breaks the trees.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَيُغْرِقَكُم بِمَا كَفَرْتُمْ ثُمَّ لاَ تَجِدُواْ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا بِهِ تَبِيعاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: an avenger.
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is from vengeance (al-thaʾr); and likewise everyone who seeks vengeance or anything else is called «تبيع» and «تابع»; and from it is His saying, the Exalted, ﴿فَاتِّبَاعٌ بالمعْرُوفِ﴾, i.e. a claim [for payment].

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِي ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلْنَاهُمْ فِي ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَرَزَقْنَاهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَاتِ وَفَضَّلْنَاهُمْ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا تَفْضِيلاً﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: they were favoured in that they eat with their hands, while the beasts eat with their mouths.
Someone else said: they were favoured with understanding and discernment, and with what has been made subservient to them.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَوْمَ نَدْعُواْ كُلَّ أُنَاسٍ بِإِمَامِهِمْْ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: i.e. by their prophet.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: by their book.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is indicated by His saying afterwards: ﴿فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ يَقْرَؤونَ كِتَابَهُمْ وَلاَ يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلاً﴾.
«الفتيل» is what is in the slit of the date-stone; «النقير» is the small hollow in it; and «القطمير» is the thin skin that is on the date-stone.
That is: they will not be wronged even the amount of this trifling thing.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَن كَانَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ أَعْمَىٰ فَهُوَ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ أَعْمَىٰ وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلاً﴾.
ʿIkrima said: "A man said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: how will he be blind in the Hereafter?
He said to him: you have mistaken the interpretation. Do you not see that He, Mighty and Majestic is He, enumerated the blessings, then said: ﴿وَمَن كَانَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ أَعْمَىٰ﴾, i.e. whoever is blind to these blessings which he sees and which point him to Allah's power, he is, with regard to what he has not seen of the matter of the Hereafter, blind." Qatāda said the same.
Someone else said: whoever was blind in this world, when Allah gave him ample span of life, promised him acceptance of repentance, and called him to obedience, yet he did not respond and was blind to that — he will be in the Hereafter, when no repentance or turning back is accepted from him, blind and further astray from the path.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
The meaning is: they almost tempted you away, because "إنَّ" and the "lām" indicate emphasis (tawkīd).
It is narrated that they said to the Prophet ﷺ: drive away from us these lowly people and clients, so that we may sit with you and listen to you; and the Prophet [ﷺ] was inclined to do so, out of his desire that they should believe; but he was protected ﷺ, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed ﴿وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ﴾ up to His saying ﴿إِذَاً لأَذَقْنَاكَ ضِعْفَ الحَيَاةِ وضِعْفَ المَمَاتِ﴾.
Mālik ibn Dīnār said: I asked Jābir ibn Zayd about His saying ﴿إِذَاً لأَذَقْنَاكَ ضِعْفَ الحَيَاةِ وضِعْفَ المَمَاتِ﴾ and he said: then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and that is its meaning according to the lexicographers. The Prophet ﷺ was addressed with this because the reward through him is abundant, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿يَا نِسَاءَ النَّبِيِّ مَنْ يَأْتِ منكنَّ بفَاحِشَةٍ يُضَاعَفْ لَهَا العَذَابُ ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾; and because the prophets witness the angels and the great signs. The benefit of that address was that it made known that this is Allah's judgement concerning whoever of the prophets disobeys Him — so how about others?
[Translator's note: the text writes «إنَّ» (with shadda) where the verse has «وَإِن» (lightened inna); translated as referring to the particle in the verse.]

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجوكَ مِنْهَا﴾.
It has been said: the meaning is: they would unsettle you by killing.
ʿAwf said, from al-Ḥasan: they resolved to drive the Prophet ﷺ out of Mecca, but Allah willed that the people of Mecca should remain, so He commanded him to leave it as an emigrant to Medina; so he left by Allah's command. Had they driven him out, they would have perished, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَإِذاً لاَّ يَلْبَثُونَ خِلافَكَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
The exegetes said: ﴿خِلاَفَكَ﴾, i.e. after you.
And it is related from the Arabs: «جاء فلانٌ خَلْفَ فلانٍ وخِلاَفَه», i.e. after him.
And "خلاف" sometimes comes in the sense of opposition.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلْلَّيْلِِ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: "its dulūk" is its setting.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, [from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ﴾ — at its setting; and al-Shaʿbī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās:] "its dulūk" is its declining from the zenith (zawāl).
Al-Zuhrī narrated from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar: ﴿دُلُوكُ الشَّمْسِ﴾ is after midday, and it is the time of ẓuhr.
Mālik and al-Layth narrated from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he said: ﴿دُلُوكُ الشَّمْسِ﴾ is its declining.
The same is narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Allah's mercy be upon him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الدُّلوك» in the language is inclining; and it [the sun] inclines at the zawāl and at setting, except that the zawāl is the more common sense of this on people's tongues.
This is indicated by the fact that after it comes ﴿إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾, so that ẓuhr, ʿaṣr, maghrib and ʿishāʾ are included in it, and after it ﴿وَقُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ﴾; and nothing prevents the ghasaq of the night from being its beginning, which is at sunset — Abū Hurayra said that.
And this strengthens the view of whoever said: al-dulūk is its inclining at the zawāl.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿غَسَقِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ is the gathering of the night and its darkness.
Qatāda said: its beginning.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ﴾.
So He called the prayer "Qurʾān" (recitation), because it is only with the Qurʾān.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُوداً﴾.
Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The dawn prayer is attended by the angels of the night and the angels of the day; recite, if you wish: ﴿وَقُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُوداً﴾."

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً لَّكََ﴾.
ʿAlqama and al-Aswad said: «التهجُّد» is [praying] after sleep.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «التهجُّد» according to the lexicographers is staying awake and keeping vigil, and «الهُجُود» is sleep; «تهجَّد» is said when he keeps vigil, and «هَجَد» when he sleeps.
It is narrated from Mujāhid that this is specifically for the Prophet ﷺ, and that the meaning of ﴿نَافِلةً لكَ﴾ is particular to the Prophet, because his sins had been forgiven him; so it is supererogatory in that he does not do it as an expiation for sins, whereas people do whatever is beyond the prescribed prayers as expiations for sins.
[Translator's note: «لا يعلمها» and «يعلمون» in the text are evidently for «لا يعملها» and «يعملون» ("does / do"); translated accordingly.]
Someone else said: ﴿نَافِلَةً لَكَ﴾, i.e. it is not an obligation, because «النَّفْل» is everything whose performance is not obligatory; and «النافلة» in the language is an addition.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿عَسَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَاماً مَّحْمُوداً﴾.
Dāwūd al-Awdī narrated from his father, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿عَسَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَاماً مَّحْمُوداً﴾ that he said: "It is the station in which I shall intercede for my community."
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: "Every «عسى» is binding."
Abū ʿUbayda said: he means in the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: it is the entry into Medina and his departure from Mecca.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is his departure from Mecca and his entry into Mecca in safety on the day of the Conquest.
Mujāhid said: it is his entry into the Message and the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱجْعَل لِّي مِن لَّدُنْكَ سُلْطَاناً نَّصِيراً﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī and ʿIkrima said: i.e. a firm proof.
Mujāhid said: i.e. a proof.
Al-Ḥasan held that it is might and victory, and the making of his religion prevail over all religion.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلْ جَآءَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلْبَاطِلُ إِنَّ ٱلْبَاطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقاً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: ﴿ٱلْحَقُّ﴾ is the Qurʾān; ﴿ٱلْبَاطِلَ﴾ is Satan; and he said: ﴿وَزَهَقَ﴾: perished.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَآءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
"مِنْ" here is not partitive; rather it is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins).
And the meaning is: and We send down what is healing and mercy for the believers; then He clarified, saying ﴿مِنَ ٱلْقُرْآنِ﴾, just as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأَوْثَانِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَآ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى ٱلإنْسَانِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَأَى بِجَانِبِهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. he kept himself far from Us.
Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read ﴿وَنَاءَ بجانبِهِ﴾, with the hamza placed after [the alif].
The first form is better known, and this one is by metathesis (qalb) of the hamza.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ كَانَ يَئُوساً﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda that he said: "يَئِسَ" means: he despaired.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: according to his intention.
Mujāhid said: i.e. according to his own way and according to his nature.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: according to his direction.
And this comes back to the view of al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid.
The true meaning — and Allah knows best — is: each one acts according to the manner to which his habit and his nature have accustomed him.
And the meaning is: it should not be so; rather the truth ought to be followed wherever it is, since the proofs have appeared and the truth has become clear.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and this comes back to the view of al-Ḥasan.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي﴾.
It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: "I was with the Prophet ﷺ and the Jews asked him about the spirit (al-rūḥ); he fell silent, and I thought he was receiving revelation, so I moved aside; then there was revealed to him ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾."
He means the Jews; and they said: we find the like of it in the Torah: (Say: the spirit is of the command of my Lord).
Abū Jaʿfar said: the scholars have spoken about the spirit:
ʿAṭāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "«الرُّوح» is an angel who has eleven thousand wings and a thousand faces, glorifying Allah until the Day of Resurrection."
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: "The rūḥ is a creation like the creation of the children of Ādam, but they are not children of Ādam; they have hands and feet."
It has also been said: the rūḥ is Jibrīl, peace be upon him; and the holder of this view argued from His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوْحُ الأَمِينُ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: and they claimed that the one who called out to them — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — was the rūḥ, Jibrīl; and the same is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: and Jibrīl stands before Allah, exalted be His praise, on the Day of Resurrection.
It has also been said: it is ʿĪsā, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, i.e. he is from the command of Allah, and not as the Christians say.
It has also been said: the rūḥ is the Qurʾān, because of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إلَيْكَ رُوحَاً مِنْ أَمْرِنَا). And Allah knows best what He intended, except that He has informed us that it is of the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
If someone says: how could it be said to the Jews {وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ when they had been given the Torah?
The answer is that "little" and "much" are known only in relation to something else; when the Torah is related to the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, it is little out of much. Do you not see His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ كَانَ البَحْرُ مِدَادَاً لِكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِد البَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْفَد كَلِمَاتُ رَبِّي، وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِ مَدَدَاً﴾!?

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِن شِئْنَا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِٱلَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾.
That is: if We willed, We would remove it from the breasts and the books.
﴿ثُمَّ لاَ تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِ عَلَيْنَا وَكِيلاً﴾, i.e. anyone who would act on your behalf in restoring it.
Al-Ḥasan said: i.e. who would protect you from Us if We intended [something against] you.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ إِنَّ فَضْلَهُ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ كَبِيراً﴾.
This is an exception not from the first [kind] (i.e. a disjoined exception), i.e. but Allah kept it firm, as a mercy and a favour from Him.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لَّئِنِ ٱجْتَمَعَتِ ٱلإِنْسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَىٰ أَن يَأْتُواْ بِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ لاَ يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيراًً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: i.e. a helper.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍِ﴾.
That is: We have directed the speech through every kind of parable; and it is from the saying: «صَرَفتُ إليك كذا», i.e. I turned it towards you.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
Then Allah informed that when they were unable to produce the like of it and their argument was cut off, they demanded signs; so He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقَالُواْ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاًً﴾.
Yet Allah had shown them signs greater than this, such as the splitting of the moon and other things.
Mujāhid said: «يَنْبُوع» is springs.
Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the lexicographers it is from «نَبَعَ، يَنْبَعُ، ويَنْبُعُ»;
and from it the estate of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, was named Yanbuʿ.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ تُسْقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفاً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: ﴿كِسَفَاً﴾: pieces.
Al-Farrāʾ related that he heard a Bedouin say: give me a «كِسْفة» of this cloth, i.e. a piece.
It is also read ﴿كِسْفَاً﴾, and the meaning on this reading refers to the whole sky, i.e. a covering layer.
And its derivation is from «كسَفْتُ الشيءَ», i.e. I covered it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ قَبِيلاً﴾.
Maʿmar and Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda that he said: ﴿قَبِيلاً﴾, i.e. face to face.
Abū Jaʿfar said: he took it to be from «المقابلة» (facing).
Someone else said: ﴿قَبِيلاً﴾, i.e. as a guarantor; one says «قَبَلتُ به», i.e. I guaranteed it, and «تقبَّل فلانٌ بكذا», i.e. he took responsibility for it.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِّن زُخْرُفٍٍ﴾.
Mujāhid narrated that he said: we did not know what «الزُّخرف» was, until we saw it in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "أو يكون لك بيتٌ من ذَهَبٍ" (or you have a house of gold).
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الزُّخرف» in the language is adornment, and gold is a form of adornment.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّى تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا كِتَاباً نَّقْرَؤُهُ﴾.
That is: a book [attesting] to your prophethood.
So Allah made known that even if that were done for them, they would not believe, and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَابَاً فِي قِرْطَاسٍ، فَلَمَسُوه بِأَيْدِيهِمْ، لَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا، إِنْ هَذَا إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوۤاْ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُوۤاْ أَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ بَشَراً رَّسُولاًً﴾.
So Allah made known that the most just and most effective [way] is that to every kind of creature should be sent one of its own kind, and He said: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ كَانَ فِي الأَرْضِ مَلاَئِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ لَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَلَكَاً رَسُولاً﴾. Then they said: who bears witness for you to this? So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدَاً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ عُمْياً وَبُكْماً وَصُمّاًً﴾.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿عُمْيَاً﴾: they see nothing that pleases them; ﴿وَبُكْمَاً﴾: they utter no argument; ﴿وَصُمَّاً﴾: they hear nothing that gladdens them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَّأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ زِدْنَاهُمْ سَعِيراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ﴾, i.e. whenever it is extinguished it is rekindled.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: whenever it subsides.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says «خَبَتِ النَّارُ» when its flame subsides; if its flame subsides and the embers turn to ash, one says «كَبَتْ»; if some of the embers are extinguished and the flame subsides, one says «خَمَدتْ»; and if it is all extinguished, one says «هَمَدتْ، تَهْمُدُ، هُمُوداً».
And the meaning of ﴿زِدْنَاهُمْ سَعِيرَاً﴾ is: We increase them in a fire that blazes (tasaʿʿaru), i.e. flares up.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لَّوْ أَنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزَآئِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي إِذاً لأمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ ٱلإِنْفَاقِِ﴾.
Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj that he said: ﴿الإِنفاق﴾ is poverty — from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: «الإنقاق» is poverty.
[Translator's note: «الإنقاق» as printed; evidently a misprint for «الإنفاق».]
The lexicographers related: «أنفَقَ», «أَصْرَمَ», «أَعدَمَ» and «أقْتَرَ» are said when a man's wealth has become little.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱلإنْسَانُ قَتُوراً﴾.
Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿قَتُورَاً﴾: miserly — from Ibn ʿAbbās.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍٍ﴾.
Shuʿba narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama, from Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl, that a Jew said to his companion: come, let us ask this prophet ﷺ. The other said to him: do not call him "prophet", for if he hears it he will have four eyes [i.e. he will be overjoyed]. He said: so he came to him and asked him about this verse ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾, and he said: "Do not associate anything with Allah; do not kill the soul which Allah has made sacred except by right; do not steal; do not commit adultery; do not consume usury; do not take an innocent person to a ruler so that he kills him; do not practise sorcery; do not flee from the advancing army; and upon you specifically, O Jews, [it is] that you do not transgress concerning the Sabbath." He said: so they kissed his hand and said: we bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. He said: then what prevents you from following me? They said: Dāwūd ﷺ prayed that there should never cease to be a prophet among his offspring, and we fear that if we follow you the Jews will kill us.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾: they are "the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the years [of drought], shortage of fruits, the hand and the staff".
This is the meaning of what they said.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَسْئَلْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read ﴿فَسَأَلَ بني إسرَائيلَ﴾.
The meaning on this reading is: so he [Moses] asked [Pharaoh for] the Children of Israel; and the meaning is: Pharaoh answered the signs and proofs that Mūsā ﷺ brought with nothing more than informing that he thought Mūsā, peace be upon him, was bewitched, and he said: ﴿إِنِّي لأَظُنُّكَ يٰمُوسَىٰ مَسْحُوراً﴾.
